To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rip current hazard and optimal escape strategies are highly variable along the beach due to differences in the alongshore dimensions and orientation of the sand bars, which determine the alongshore variability in flow regime.
the best rip current escape strategies vary alongshore and are dependent on the flow field and the bar/rip channel morphology.

rip current hazard and optimal rip current escape strategies are highly variable along open beaches, and this alongshore variability is strongly influenced by subtle differences in the morphology of the rip channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the variability of rip current escape strategy alongshore, which is an important factor in the definition of rip current hazard and in turn, the design and communication of rip current escape messages to the general public.
the development of a rip current safety strategy for a multiple rip-channel beach, which is a common feature of many rip-channelled beaches worldwide.
improving the safety of beach-goers by providing a scientific basis to develop beach safety messages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

“stay afloat, swim parallel to shore, and then swim towards shore with breaking waves” is the best rip current escape message on open beaches, with the caveat that this is only true for obliquely incident wave conditions and rip channels with a large alongshore spacing.

the best rip current escape strategies depend upon wave direction and rip flow regime (dominance of surf-zone exit versus recirculation), and that these two parameters are highly variable along a multiple rip-channel beach.
the best rip current escape strategies for open rip-channelled beach environments depend on the alongshore location, wave conditions and the rip flow regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alongshore variability in optimum rip current escape strategy on open rip-channel beaches is large and is dependent on subtle differences in bar and rip morphology.
rip current hazard and optimum rip current escape strategy is highly dependent on wave incidence, rip spacing and bar/rip morphology, which in turn is highly variable alongshore.
the optimal escape strategy is highly variable alongshore and is influenced by the flow regime, rip velocity and bar/rip morphology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best rip current escape message should take into account the local beach morphology and flow field, which can change from one rip system (and even rip channel) to another.

beach safety practitioners need to be aware that rip current hazard and escape strategy are highly dependent on the alongshore bar/rip morphology and wave incidence, and therefore should tailor their safety message to local conditions.
the optimal rip current safety message should be tailored to the local rip channel morphology.
